scope: Owned C-Gate 3.4.0 build 2001 classfile semantics, retained original routed RECALL and IDENTIFY correlation matrices, CBUS-SIUG source routing, and cmqttd scripted one-through-six-bridge acceptance; no live C-Bus bridge or site data

selected_native_runtime.classfile_tool: javap from the pinned owned Java 11 runtime

native_classfile_findings.finding: The command registry maps set_project_identify to kS.

runCommand resolves exactly one supplied address with argAsNetworkList, casts the result only to CBusBaseNetwork, encodes the uppercase one-to-eight-character identity to six bytes, and invokes CBusBaseNetwork.a(access, encoded). It contains no direct-network or concrete-network-class restriction.

The method requires six encoded bytes, selects the first usable nonzero-address unit through the addressed network's own MMI and identity machinery, then calls CBusUnit.a(access, encoded) on that unit.

The unit method binds a ct STORE command to the same CBusBaseNetwork and calls ct.a(unit, 35, 70, six bytes, 6): parameter 35 and decimal 70/fixed tag 0x46. It waits for completion and distinguishes no-response, negative acknowledge and other store failure. Native does not perform a second parameter-35 readback here; cmqttd deliberately requires one before updating its cache.

Bridge networks are CBusBaseNetwork instances and use their near-side chain for command transport. Because kS retains the resolved base-network object through unit selection and STORE binding, the native command contract includes a resolved bridged network rather than substituting the root network.

retained_route_evidence.finding: Original C-Gate receiver correlation accepts Reply Network paths from one through six bridges and rejects route, unit and CAL mismatches across the finite retained matrix.
Original routed IDENTIFY matching establishes the same Reply Network envelope used to select the destination unit safely before STORE.
The retained native topology acceptance pins CBusBridgeNetwork resolution and the one-to-six source-route bound.

cmqttd_acceptance: Transport tests pin literal one- and six-bridge STORE and RECALL frames, exact Reply Network/unit/parameter/tag correlation, exact readback, route-length validation and retirement without replay after mismatched readback.

Service tests run routed MMI, IDENTIFY1 and the complete IDENTIFY4 uniqueness window, reject direct and neighbouring-route replies, send one STORE, require routed readback, and update only the target network's volatile ProjectName; a mismatched readback retires the generation without replay, invalidates only the target value, and preserves the root-network cache.
A real cmqttd test completes the routed mutation while direct lighting observations continue to reach MQTT over the same single CNI connection.
evidence_boundaries: No physical bridge or routed unit completed this mutation in the acceptance run.

The original classfile proves bridged-network admission and the STORE selector. Literal routed STORE bytes are implementation acceptance from the selected native command contract, CBUS-SIUG routing grammar and retained routed-correlation matrices, not a native wire capture of this exact command.
cmqttd's exact RECALL verification is a stricter commit rule than the selected native C-Gate method and does not claim device persistence or power-cycle survival.
An incomplete or mismatched routed write retires the shared PCI generation and is never retried automatically.
